problems.text: Customer support is expensive (stated by the VP Product, no figure given)
The VP Product says the support team spends all day on repetitive questions; this has not been checked with support

proposed_solutions.text: Build an AI chatbot to handle customer support automatically

user_segments.text: The support team, which the VP Product says answers repetitive questions all day

requests.text: The chatbot would answer support questions such as how to reschedule a meeting and which calendar systems are supported
VP Product wants a prototype by end of Q4
VP Product's reason to act: competition is shipping chatbots and "we need to keep up"

decisions.text: PM to gather data first: the support ticket breakdown and whether there is actual demand from customers
Revisit in two weeks once the PM has numbers; VP Product agreed

open_questions.text: How many support tickets are there per question type? The VP Product does not know the exact breakdown
Is there actual demand from customers for a chatbot?
What is the support team actually spending its time on? The VP Product has not talked to support yet

action_items.text: PM to check with support on their top issues
PM to get the support ticket breakdown and see if there is actual demand from customers

metrics_mentioned.text: Support tickets: "maybe a few hundred per month", a guess by the VP Product
Engineer Lead: a few hundred is pretty thin if the chatbot must handle diverse questions reliably
